One moves a customs fee date by one week, to October 7, 2017. The other raises a corporate tax payment rate by a quarter of a point. The whole measure took effect by July 29, 2008 at the latest.
plaw-110-288-2008:
Pleasure boats need no discharge permit for everyday waste water under Public Law 110-288. It is the Clean Boating Act of 2008, approved on July 29, 2008. The act amends the Federal Water Pollution Control Act.

The rule covers graywater, bilge water, cooling water, and deck runoff. It also covers outflow from oil separators and from marine engines that work as they should. A covered boat is one made or used mainly for pleasure, or rented out for pleasure. Work boats that carry paying riders are left out. A part on care practices follows, past the sample's end.
plaw-110-289-2008:
Housing finance gets a new watchdog in Public Law 110-289, approved on July 30, 2008. It is the Housing and Economic Recovery Act of 2008. Its purpose line promises needed housing reform.

The contents list opens with a part on housing finance reform. Its first title sets up the Federal Housing Finance Agency and an oversight board. It lists the director's duties, reporting powers, and exam staff. Standards follow for safe operations, for holdings and debts, and for capital levels. One item puts the watched firms under the securities laws. The sample ends within that first title's list.
plaw-110-290-2008: Funds for a rules review body are renewed by Public Law 110-290, the Regulatory Improvement Act of 2007. Approved on July 30, 2008, the act covers the Administrative Conference of the United States. It allows up to a set sum for each of the fiscal years 2009, 2010, and 2011. Of that money, only a small slice may go to hosting foreign guests each year. The sums are stated in the act in dollars, year by year.
plaw-110-291-2008: Bus firms must meet access rules to win registration, under Public Law 110-291. Approved on July 30, 2008, it is the Over-the-Road Bus Transportation Accessibility Act of 2007. A carrier of passengers may be registered only if willing and able to meet access rules set by the transport chief. The rules cited are a named part of the federal rule book, or any later rules that replace them. Matching words are added in two more parts of the transport code. A definition part begins as the sample ends.
plaw-110-292-2008: Ponce, Puerto Rico names a veterans clinic in Public Law 110-292, approved on July 30, 2008. The outpatient clinic there is designated the Euripides Rubio Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic. The whole act is a single section. It adds that any mention of the clinic in a federal law, rule, map, or record counts as a mention of the clinic by the Rubio name.
plaw-110-293-2008:
World fights against three diseases are funded again by Public Law 110-293, approved on July 30, 2008. Its long title names Tom Lantos and Henry J. Hyde, and the United States Global Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Reauthorization Act of 2008. The act covers aid for fiscal years 2009 through 2013.

The contents list starts with planning. It calls for an updated five year global plan and a joint agency work group. A second title backs shared funds and partnerships. Items cover vaccine funds, the Global Fund, and studies on ways women can block HIV spread. The sample ends within that title.
plaw-110-294-2008: Justice grants keep their 2006 funding level through 2012 under Public Law 110-294. Approved on July 30, 2008, the act covers the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant Program. It strikes words in the 1968 crime control act that set funds for fiscal year 2006. In their place it sets funds for each of the fiscal years 2006 through 2012. That date swap is the whole act.
plaw-110-295-2008:
Leftover funds may teach viewers about digital television under Public Law 110-295. Approved on July 30, 2008, it is called the DTV Transition Assistance Act. Its purpose line calls it a technical correction to a 2005 deficit law, though the text amends a television act of 2005.

An assistant secretary must judge whether the full sum set for payments will be needed. If not, the rest may fund teaching and help on the switch to digital broadcasts. Help may run through nonprofit and public interest groups, by grants or contracts. A plan must serve seniors, rural viewers, and minorities first in line.
plaw-110-296-2008: Background checks for volunteers get six more months from Public Law 110-296, approved on July 30, 2008. It is the Criminal History Background Checks Pilot Extension Act of 2008. The act extends a test program that lets volunteer groups obtain criminal history checks. The change is a number swap in the PROTECT Act. A sixty month span becomes a sixty-six month span. Nothing else in the program is changed by this text.
plaw-110-297-2008:
A tribal water settlement in California is approved by Public Law 110-297, approved on July 31, 2008. It is the Soboba Band of Luiseno Indians Settlement Act. The Interior chief is told to sign and carry out the deal, per the purpose line.

The findings set out the claim. The tribe's reservation, about six thousand acres by the San Jacinto River, dates to an order of 1883. Its water rights were never measured in court. The tribe sued a big water district in 2000, blaming a tunnel for harm to its water. Claims against two nearby districts are noted as the sample ends.
plaw-110-298-2008:
Bravery badges for police officers are set up by Public Law 110-298, approved on July 31, 2008. It is the Law Enforcement Congressional Badge of Bravery Act of 2008. Its purpose line promises an awards path for rare brave acts in the line of duty, at all levels of policing.

The part shown is all definitions. A federal officer is a worker with power to arrest, who may carry a gun. The job must center on stopping, solving, or punishing crime, or on guard work. Boards and badges for the federal side are also defined. The sample ends within the state officer terms.
plaw-110-299-2008:
Small boats get a two year permit break in Public Law 110-299, approved on July 31, 2008. The act clarifies when permits may be required for discharges from certain vessels. It also orders a study of discharges tied to normal vessel use, per its title.

A covered vessel is under seventy-nine feet long, or is a fishing vessel of any length. For two years, no federal permit is needed for engine outflow that works as it should. Laundry, shower, and galley sink waste are covered too. Trash and garbage thrown overboard are left out, the text states. The sample ends within the exceptions.
plaw-110-300-2008: Two weeks, not a month, is the span granted by Public Law 110-300, approved on July 31, 2008. The act extends programs under the Higher Education Act of 1965 for a short time. It changes the date in the 2005 extension law from July 31, 2008 to August 15, 2008. The change counts as if made on July 31 itself. A guard clause protects funds and spans set by three earlier laws on aid and loans.
plaw-110-301-2008:
Claims against Libya by Americans are aimed at settlement in Public Law 110-301, approved on August 4, 2008. It is the Libyan Claims Resolution Act. The part shown gives definitions and a statement of support from Congress.

A claims agreement, in the act, is a binding deal between the two countries. It must settle terror related claims of United States nationals against Libya, through fair payment. Congress backs the President in seeking such a deal for all claimants. The text ties that search to restoring normal ties between the two nations. Later parts of the act lie past the sample.
plaw-110-302-2008: Wenatchee, Washington names a veterans clinic in Public Law 110-302, approved on August 12, 2008. The outpatient clinic there is designated the Elwood 'Bud' Link Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic. The references part then speaks of the medical center named above, though the part before it names a clinic. Later mentions in federal laws and records are read under the Link name.
plaw-110-303-2008: Weldon, North Carolina names a post office building in Public Law 110-303, approved on August 12, 2008. The site at 401 Washington Avenue is designated the Dock M. Brown Post Office Building. Under part two, a mention of that site in any federal law, map, or record is deemed a mention of the Brown building by name.
plaw-110-304-2008: Miami's veterans medical center takes a name in Public Law 110-304, approved on August 12, 2008. The center in Florida is designated the Bruce W. Carter Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center. The act is one section long. It adds that a mention of the center in any federal law, rule, map, or record counts as a mention of the center by the Carter name.
plaw-110-305-2008: San Gabriel, California names a post office building in Public Law 110-305, approved on August 12, 2008. The Postal Service site at 120 South Del Mar Avenue is designated the Chi Mui Post Office Building. References to that site in federal laws, maps, and records are then deemed references to the building under the Mui name.
plaw-110-306-2008: Oakton, Virginia honors a private first class in Public Law 110-306, approved on August 12, 2008. The post office at 10449 White Granite Drive is designated the Private First Class David H. Sharrett II Post Office Building. The act then deems a mention of that site, in any federal law or record, to be a mention of the Sharrett building.
plaw-110-307-2008: Charlottesville honors a corporal in Public Law 110-307, approved on August 12, 2008. The Postal Service site at 1155 Seminole Trail in Virginia is designated the Corporal Bradley T. Arms Post Office Building. References to that site in federal laws, maps, and records are read as references to the building by the Arms name.
plaw-110-308-2008: West Frankfort, Illinois names a post office building in Public Law 110-308, approved on August 12, 2008. The site at 219 East Main Street is designated the Kenneth James Gray Post Office Building. Part two of the act makes later federal citations of that site stand as citations of the Gray building by its full name.
plaw-110-309-2008: Rancho Mirage names a post office for a former president in Public Law 110-309. Approved on August 12, 2008, the act covers the site at 42222 Rancho Las Palmas Drive in California. It is designated the Gerald R. Ford Post Office Building. A mention of that site in a federal law, map, or other record is deemed a mention of the Ford building.
plaw-110-310-2008: Cleveland, Ohio names a post office building in Public Law 110-310, approved on August 12, 2008. The site at 14500 Lorain Avenue is designated the John P. Gallagher Post Office Building. The act's second part reads a citation of that site, in a federal law or record, as a citation of the Gallagher building instead.
plaw-110-311-2008: White Plains names a courthouse in Public Law 110-311, approved on August 12, 2008. The federal building and courthouse at 300 Quarropas Street in New York are designated for Charles L. Brieant, Jr. The full new name is the Charles L. Brieant, Jr., Federal Building and United States Courthouse. Federal records citing the site then cite that name.
plaw-110-312-2008: The parole board's work is kept going by Public Law 110-312, approved on August 12, 2008. Its short title is the United States Parole Commission Extension Act of 2008. The act works by a deemed reading of an older law. In the Sentencing Reform Act of 1984, each mention of twenty-one years, for the parole part of title 18, is read as twenty-four years. That reading covers the commission itself.
plaw-110-313-2008:
Who names patent and trademark judges is shifted by Public Law 110-313, approved on August 12, 2008. The title states the new rule. The commerce chief names such judges, after consulting the head of the Patent and Trademark Office.

For patent judges, the text swaps the naming power from the director to the commerce chief. Past judges named by the director may be treated as named on their first day. A challenge based on that old route fails if the judge acted as a de facto officer, the act adds. A trademark part follows in like terms.
plaw-110-314-2008:
Children's goods get stricter safety rules in Public Law 110-314, approved on August 14, 2008. It is the Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act of 2008. Its purpose line also promises to renew and update the product safety agency.

The first title covers lead in children's goods and a lead paint rule. It orders outside testing for some goods, tracking labels, and rules for nursery goods that last. Toy safety standards are made binding, and one part bans some goods with named chemicals. A study of harm to minority children is listed. The sample ends as agency reforms begin.
plaw-110-315-2008:
College law is amended and extended by Public Law 110-315, approved on August 14, 2008. It is the Higher Education Opportunity Act. The act rewrites parts of the Higher Education Act of 1965, the main federal college aid law.

The opening title sets broad terms. It defines what counts as a college for aid programs and guards student speech and group rights. Items cover drug and alcohol prevention, diploma mills, and clearer tuition facts for buyers. Textbook facts, in state tuition for service families, and a bar on a student data bank are listed too. The sample ends there.
plaw-110-316-2008:
Fees on animal drugs are revised and extended by Public Law 110-316, approved on August 14, 2008. The act amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. Its contents list runs to three titles.

The first title covers the animal drug user fee program, with power to charge and use the fees. It adds reports on how widely germ drugs are handed out. The second title sets fees for copycat animal drugs, with reports and end dates. The third title makes technical corrections to a 2007 food and drug law. It covers petitions and a results data bank.
plaw-110-317-2008:
Fair terms for sole surviving service members are set by Public Law 110-317, approved on August 29, 2008. It is called the Hubbard Act. The discharge at issue goes to the only child left in a family where service cost a parent or sibling their life, health, or freedom.

The contents list keeps bonuses and like benefits paid after such a discharge. It adds separation pay, short term health care, and store benefits on base. Jobless pay and hiring preference are covered too. A last item lifts a cap on sums paid into funeral trusts, in the tax code.
plaw-110-318-2008: The Highway Trust Fund is topped up by Public Law 110-318, approved on September 15, 2008. The act amends the tax code section that tracks the fund's balance. Most of its text moves and renumbers parts of that section. The core act is one new paragraph. It sets aside a sum in the billions, from Treasury money not already assigned, for the fund. A matching fix swaps one word in a nearby sentence, and the act took effect on approval.
plaw-110-319-2008: Brooklyn names a courthouse for a former president in Public Law 110-319. Approved on September 17, 2008, the act covers the courthouse at 225 Cadman Plaza East in New York. It is designated the Theodore Roosevelt United States Courthouse. The second part deems a mention of that courthouse, in any federal law or record, to be a mention under the Roosevelt name.
plaw-110-320-2008: Richmond names a courthouse for two men in Public Law 110-320, approved on September 18, 2008. The courthouse stands in the 700 block of East Broad Street in Virginia, with no exact number given. It is designated the Spottswood W. Robinson III and Robert R. Merhige, Jr., United States Courthouse. Federal records citing that courthouse then cite the two name form.
plaw-110-321-2008:
State Department powers are extended in several small ways by Public Law 110-321, approved on September 19, 2008. The act opens with rehiring of retired foreign service staff. A year in that rule moves from 2008 to 2009.

Rest and recovery travel now counts the territories by name, from American Samoa to the Virgin Islands. Pay for food and lodging now covers guards on protection duty at or away from their posts. Radio Free Asia gains a year, to 2010. A part on staff powers for world broadcasting begins as the sample ends. Each change is brief and dated.
plaw-110-322-2008:
Limits on losing legal privilege by sharing are set by Public Law 110-322, approved on September 19, 2008. The act adds a new rule, Rule 502, to the Federal Rules of Evidence. It covers lawyer client privilege and work product cover.

A sharing in a federal case waives cover for hidden items only on three tests. The waiver must be meant, the items must share a topic, and fairness must call for reading them together. A slip does not waive cover if fair steps were taken to stop it, and to fix it fast. A state case part follows, past the sample's end.
plaw-110-323-2008:
Reforms at the government's audit office are made by Public Law 110-323, approved on September 22, 2008. It is the Government Accountability Office Act of 2008. Amendments in the act are to title 31, unless a part says otherwise.

The contents list is mostly about pay and staff rules. It covers future yearly pay changes and pay for past years. It adds a lump sum tied to work based pay, and an inspector general for the office. Other items cover audit cost repayment, money disclosure by staff, and the top basic pay rate. The sample ends as the pay detail begins.
plaw-110-324-2008:
Veterans' pay rates rise with living costs under Public Law 110-324, approved on September 24, 2008. It is the Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2008. The act writes into law the rises that took effect on December 1, 2007, and adds a new one for December 1, 2008.

The sums to be raised are listed by type. They cover wartime disability pay and added pay for dependents. A clothing allowance is named. So are payments to a surviving spouse and to children of certain disabled veterans who died. The sample ends as the rise's size is set.
plaw-110-325-2008:
Broad cover under the disability rights law is restored, in aim, by Public Law 110-325. Approved on September 25, 2008, it is the ADA Amendments Act of 2008. Its purpose line promises to restore the intent and protections of the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990.

The findings say Congress meant a clear, wide ban on bias against people with disabilities. They say court rulings since then cut that scope down. Two Supreme Court cases are named, from 1999 and 2002. As a result, the act states, lower courts wrongly found many people with strong limits to be outside the law. The sample ends in the findings.
plaw-110-326-2008:
Former vice presidents gain short term guarding in Public Law 110-326, approved on September 26, 2008. Title one is the Former Vice President Protection Act of 2008. Title two, shown only by its heading, is an identity theft act.

The Secret Service must guard a former vice president, a spouse, and children under sixteen. The cover runs for no more than six months after the leader leaves office. The homeland security chief may order more cover later, if facts or conditions call for it. The rule covers any vice president in office on or after approval day.
plaw-110-327-2008: Need based college aid gets favorable antitrust treatment for longer under Public Law 110-327. Approved on September 30, 2008, it is the Need-Based Educational Aid Act of 2008. The catalog title calls the treatment permanent. The text itself does less. It strikes one year in the Improving America's Schools Act of 1994, 2008, and puts in 2015. The favor is extended, not made endless.
plaw-110-328-2008:
Income aid for older and disabled refugees runs longer under Public Law 110-328, approved on September 30, 2008. It is the SSI Extension for Elderly and Disabled Refugees Act. The act also covers collecting jobless pay debts gained by fraud, per its purpose line.

The part shown stretches a time limit in the 1996 welfare law. For set groups, a seven year span counts as nine years during fiscal years 2009 through 2011. The groups named are qualified aliens and victims of trafficking. A signed statement to the Social Security chief is required, the text adds. The sample ends mid rule.
plaw-110-329-2008:
Five spending bills are packed into Public Law 110-329, approved on September 30, 2008. Its short title is the Consolidated Security, Disaster Assistance, and Continuing Appropriations Act, 2009. The bill's own opening line still speaks of homeland security funds for a year just ending, a lag behind its 2009 title.

The contents list names the five parts. They are a stopgap funding part for 2009, a disaster relief part for 2008, and full year parts for defense, homeland security, and military building with veterans affairs. A note adds that a reference to this act, inside a part, means that part alone.
plaw-110-330-2008: Airport taxes run into 2009 under Public Law 110-330, approved on September 30, 2008. It is the Federal Aviation Administration Extension Act of 2008, Part II. Fuel and ticket taxes now end on March 31, 2009, not September 30, 2008. The power to spend from the airport trust fund runs to April 1, 2009. The tax changes took effect on October 1, 2008. The purpose line also promises a longer run for airport improvement grants.
plaw-110-331-2008: Commerce, Oklahoma names a post office for a baseball great in Public Law 110-331. Approved on September 30, 2008, the act covers the site at 301 Commerce Street, a fitting road name. It is designated the Mickey Mantle Post Office Building. Later mentions of that site in federal laws, maps, and records are deemed mentions of the Mantle building by name.
plaw-110-332-2008: Alpena, Michigan names a veterans clinic in Public Law 110-332, approved on September 30, 2008. The clinic there is designated the Lieutenant Colonel Clement C. Van Wagoner Department of Veterans Affairs Clinic. The act adds that a mention of the clinic in any federal law, rule, map, or record counts as a mention of the clinic by the Van Wagoner name.
plaw-110-333-2008: Fort Pierce, Florida names a post office building in Public Law 110-333, approved on September 30, 2008. The Postal Service site at 1717 Orange Avenue is designated the CeeCee Ross Lyles Post Office Building. Under part two, federal records that point to that site point to it under the Lyles name from approval onward.
plaw-110-334-2008: Omaha names a bureau building still being built in Public Law 110-334, approved on October 1, 2008. The Federal Bureau of Investigation building rises at the crossing of 120th and L Streets in Nebraska, an address the text gives. It is designated the J. James Exon Federal Bureau of Investigation Building. Federal records citing the building then cite the Exon name.
plaw-110-335-2008: Pay for lawyers who defend poor clients in the capital's courts rises under Public Law 110-335. Approved on October 2, 2008, the act carries out a raise set in a 2008 spending law. The hourly rate moves from sixty-five dollars to eighty dollars. Caps on total pay for a case are reset to match the federal caps for like work. The new terms cover Superior Court cases, appeals, and matters after trial. They apply to cases begun on or after approval day.
plaw-110-336-2008:
Saving old recordings and films at the Library of Congress is funded again by Public Law 110-336. Approved on October 2, 2008, it is the Library of Congress Sound Recording and Film Preservation Programs Reauthorization Act of 2008.

For the recording board, the funding span is restated to run through fiscal year 2016. That change counts as if it sat in the 2000 act from the start. The Librarian may now drop a board member who misses set meetings, after fair notice, without sending a stand-in. The same may be done for a member who fails the job in a large way.
plaw-110-337-2008: Airport fees may pay to quiet a school near a big airport under Public Law 110-337, approved on October 2, 2008. The act widens what passenger facility fees may cover, in title 49. The case is narrow. The airport must be a large hub bound by a 1980 court order in Los Angeles. The work must cut noise in a school building that the transport chief finds hurt by airport noise. Swapping a movable building for a fixed one is allowed, with costs capped at the build itself.
plaw-110-338-2008:
The Kennedy Center gains funds and a solar study in Public Law 110-338, approved on October 3, 2008. It is the John F. Kennedy Center Reauthorization Act of 2008. A small fix first swaps a House panel's old name for its current one.

The board may study, plan, and build a solar power system for the center's main roof. Before building starts, it must report on the plan to two panels of Congress. Yearly sums for upkeep, repair, and security are then listed, starting with the fiscal years 2008 and 2009. The sample ends within that list of sums.
plaw-110-339-2008:
Grants for healthy starts in life are reshaped by Public Law 110-339, approved on October 3, 2008. It is the Healthy Start Reauthorization Act of 2007, despite the later approval year. The act deals with the Healthy Start Initiative in the Public Health Service Act.

Grant makers must weigh what drives infant deaths, such as low birth weight. They must weigh how well a bidder pulls a whole town into the work. Full care for women's health, to better birth outcomes, counts as well. Grants for special projects are protected. They target gaps along the Mexico border, and in Alaska and Hawaii. The sample ends early.
plaw-110-340-2008:
Using children as soldiers is made a federal crime by Public Law 110-340, approved on October 3, 2008. It is the Child Soldiers Accountability Act of 2008. Its purpose line also bars entry to, and allows removal of, people who do such recruiting.

The crime covers a person who knowingly signs up a child under fifteen for an armed force or group. It also covers using such a child to take an active part in fighting. The penalty runs to twenty years in prison, or life if a death results. United States courts may hear a case where the accused is a citizen or a lawful resident, the text states.
plaw-110-341-2008: A telescope array in Arizona gets a new home site in Public Law 110-341, approved on October 3, 2008. The joint resolution amends a 2004 law on the VERITAS project. In the older law's title, words placing the work on Kitt Peak near Tucson are cut. The new title places the project in Arizona as a whole. In the text, the site becomes the Fred Lawrence Whipple Observatory Base Camp on Mount Hopkins, or a like place.
plaw-110-342-2008: Great Lakes water gains a shared rule book in Public Law 110-342, approved on October 3, 2008. The joint resolution gives the consent of Congress to a compact among eight states. They are Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, New York, Ohio, Wisconsin, and Pennsylvania. The compact covers water resources in the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence River Basin. The text shown sets out the compact itself, opening with its title and a long list of defined terms.
plaw-110-343-2008:
Banks in crisis are the subject of Public Law 110-343, approved on October 3, 2008. The catalog title names the whole act for its first part, the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act of 2008. The wider purpose line adds energy breaks, tax extensions, and relief for single taxpayers.

Division A sets up a Troubled Assets Relief Program. The government may buy or insure troubled assets, under a new oversight board. Parts cover reports, contract rules, and clashes of interest. Help for homeowners and curbs on top pay at aided firms are listed too. One aim named is to keep long term costs to taxpayers low. The sample ends there.
plaw-110-344-2008:
Old civil rights murders get a fresh push for answers in Public Law 110-344, approved on October 7, 2008. It is the Emmett Till Unsolved Civil Rights Crime Act of 2007. Congress states that all who hold power in such cases should act fast, since time has passed and witnesses are aging.

The Attorney General must name a deputy chief in the Civil Rights Division's criminal part. That deputy coordinates work on rights crimes that took place by the end of 1969 and ended in a death. State and local police may be drawn in. A yearly study of the cases is required.
plaw-110-345-2008: Grants for children put at risk by drugs run two years longer under Public Law 110-345. Approved on October 7, 2008, the Drug Endangered Children Act of 2007 extends the grant program of that name. It changes a span in a 2005 patriot act renewal law. The years fiscal 2006 and 2007 become fiscal 2008 and 2009. That single line is the whole act.
plaw-110-346-2008:
Rights in North Korea are taken up again by Public Law 110-346, approved on October 7, 2008. It is the North Korean Human Rights Reauthorization Act of 2008. The act amends the 2004 law of the same theme.

The findings call the 2004 act a product of broad support in both parties. They note two million Korean Americans, many with family ties to the North. Conditions inside North Korea are called deplorable, and refugees acutely at risk. China is said to hunt and return border crossers by force, who then face torture, jail, or death. The sample ends within the findings.
plaw-110-347-2008: Waterville, New York honors a corporal in Public Law 110-347, approved on October 7, 2008. The post office at 101 West Main Street is designated the Cpl. John P. Sigsbee Post Office. The act's second part then deems later mentions of that site, in a federal law or record, to be mentions of the Sigsbee post office.
plaw-110-348-2008: Bremen, Georgia honors a sergeant in Public Law 110-348, approved on October 7, 2008. The Postal Service site at 101 Tallapoosa Street is designated the Sergeant Paul Saylor Post Office Building. References to that site in federal laws, maps, and other records are read as references to the building by the Saylor name after approval.
plaw-110-349-2008: Odessa, Texas honors a corporal in Public Law 110-349, approved on October 7, 2008. The post office at 200 North Texas Avenue is designated the Corporal Alfred Mac Wilson Post Office. Under the act, a later mention of that site in a federal law, map, or record counts as a mention of the Wilson post office.
plaw-110-350-2008: Student loan buying power gains a year under Public Law 110-350, approved on October 7, 2008. The title states its aim, to extend the education chief's power to purchase guaranteed student loans. Dates in the Higher Education Act move by one year throughout. A July 2009 date becomes July 2010, and a September date moves in step. A second part extends the power to name lenders of last resort, on like one year shifts.
plaw-110-351-2008:
Foster children and their kin are the focus of Public Law 110-351, approved on October 7, 2008. It is the Fostering Connections to Success and Increasing Adoptions Act of 2008. The act amends parts of title IV of the Social Security Act.

The first title backs relatives who take in children. It lists payments for kin guardians, family connection grants, and a duty to notify relatives. Licensing rules for relatives follow. A second title seeks better outcomes in foster care. It lists a state choice to keep some youth past age eighteen, plans for aging out, school stability, and keeping siblings together.
plaw-110-352-2008: Lakeview, Oregon names a post office building in Public Law 110-352, approved on October 7, 2008. The Postal Service site at 18 S. G Street is designated the Dr. Bernard Daly Post Office Building. The naming clause is printed without the usual words shall be known and designated, an apparent slip in the enrolled text. The references part then reads federal mentions of the site as mentions of the Daly building.
plaw-110-353-2008: Kansas City, Missouri names a post office building in Public Law 110-353, approved on October 7, 2008. The site at 1700 Cleveland Avenue is designated the Reverend Earl Abel Post Office Building. Part two of the act deems a mention of that site, in any federal law or record, to be a mention of the building by the Abel name.
plaw-110-354-2008:
Links between breast cancer and the world around us are studied under Public Law 110-354. Approved on October 8, 2008, it is the Breast Cancer and Environmental Research Act of 2008. Its purpose line backs grants for centers that study such factors.

Within six months, the health chief must set up a joint panel on the topic. The panel shares news of work in hand and urges ways to improve it. It must also build a full plan and advise the health institutes on seeking new study bids. The sample ends as that plan duty is spelled out.
plaw-110-355-2008:
Community health centers gain larger sums under Public Law 110-355, approved on October 8, 2008. It is the Health Care Safety Net Act of 2008. The act adds funding authority for the health centers program in the Public Health Service Act.

The sums rise year by year. They start at just over two billion dollars for fiscal year 2008. They end at just over three billion dollars for fiscal year 2012. A second part orders studies of the centers. The first study named covers school based health centers, with a report due within two years. The sample ends there.
plaw-110-356-2008:
Firms run by people with felony records are barred from guard work under Public Law 110-356. Approved on October 8, 2008, it is the Federal Protective Service Guard Contracting Reform Act of 2008.

The homeland security chief must write rules for the ban, through the immigration enforcement chief. The rules may set permanent or interim bars. They must name which serious felonies may block a firm. Bidders must report past felony records that count. Officers who award contracts get guides for weighing risk, past fault, and present fitness, and may still award in set cases.
plaw-110-357-2008:
A silver dollar honors Army infantry in Public Law 110-357, approved on October 8, 2008. It is the National Infantry Museum and Soldier Center Commemorative Coin Act. The Treasury chief must mint the coins, in honor of the infantry's legacy and of the new museum.

No more than a set cap of one dollar coins may be made. Each is mostly silver, with a fixed weight and width stated in the act. The coins are legal tender and count as collector items. Their design must speak of the courage, pride, sacrifice, duty, and history of the infantry. A year and the word Liberty must appear.
plaw-110-358-2008:
Cases against child pornography are made easier to bring by Public Law 110-358, approved on October 8, 2008. The act amends title 18, the criminal code. Its contents list splits the work into two titles with like names.

The first title clarifies the ban on such material. The second title adds money laundering as a linked charge. It also covers a person who knowingly seeks out such material in order to view it. The findings call the trade a multibillion dollar world industry, sped by the internet. Most holders held images of children under twelve, the act states.
plaw-110-359-2008:
A grand old building on Pennsylvania Avenue is set for new life by Public Law 110-359. Approved on October 8, 2008, it is the Old Post Office Building Redevelopment Act of 2008. The services chief may provide for the building's redevelopment.

The building stands at 1100 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW, in the capital, with its Pavilion Annex. The findings call it a valuable, historic site in the heart of the city. A House panel had pressed for years over its waste and neglect, they state. Selling it may be hard, the act adds, since it sits close to the White House. A redevelopment plan was filed in the year 2000.
plaw-110-360-2008: DNA testing backlogs gain funds again under Public Law 110-360, approved on October 8, 2008. It is the Debbie Smith Reauthorization Act of 2008. The act renews the grant program named for Debbie Smith in a 2000 backlog law. A yearly sum is set for the Attorney General for fiscal years 2009 through 2014. At least forty percent of grant money in later years must go to one named use. Training and exam grant spans are also moved, to run through 2014.
plaw-110-361-2008:
Muscular dystrophy research is widened by Public Law 110-361, approved on October 8, 2008. Its long name is the Paul D. Wellstone Muscular Dystrophy Community Assistance, Research, and Education Amendments of 2008. The act covers the many forms of the disease named in its purpose line.

One more health institute joins the joint work, the heart, lung, and blood institute. The centers of excellence gain a name, the Paul D. Wellstone Muscular Dystrophy Cooperative Research Centers. A panel may weigh whether more lab and clinic capacity is needed to test new cures. A part on the disease control agency's tracking work follows.
plaw-110-362-2008: Doctors trained abroad get a longer waiver window in Public Law 110-362, approved on October 8, 2008. The catalog title calls the span five years. The text itself moves one date, from June 1, 2008 to March 6, 2009. A second part doubles a number in the Conrad State 30 Program, from five to ten. Congress adds that such waiver programs aim to bring care to places that lack doctors. Health officials should weigh poor towns and high infant death rates in naming shortage areas.
plaw-110-363-2008:
A coin marks one hundred years of the Boy Scouts in Public Law 110-363, approved on October 8, 2008. It is the Boy Scouts of America Centennial Commemorative Coin Act. The Treasury chief must mint the coins for the milestone.

The findings date the centennial to February 8, 2010. The group is called the largest youth body in the country, with millions of youth and adult leaders. Over one hundred million youth have taken part since 1910, the act states. A federal charter came in 1916. The mission, oath, and law of the Scouts are quoted at length. Service hours by Scouts run to millions in four years.
plaw-110-364-2008:
Surplus Coast Guard land in Oregon passes to tribal trust in Public Law 110-364, approved on October 8, 2008. It is the Oregon Surplus Federal Land Act of 2008. The land goes to the Confederated Tribes of the Coos, Lower Umpqua, and Siuslaw Indians.

Within five years, the Coast Guard chief must hand control of the land to the Interior chief. The Interior chief holds it in trust for the tribes. The land covers about twenty-four acres in Coos County, at Gregory Point and nearby ground. A light station on Chief's Island is defined in the act. The sample ends within the land account.
plaw-110-365-2008: Dirty sediment in the Great Lakes gets cleanup rules again under Public Law 110-365. Approved on October 8, 2008, the Great Lakes Legacy Reauthorization Act of 2008 amends the water pollution law. It adds two defined terms. Site characterization means the process of testing how far sediment harm spreads, under agency guidance. A potentially responsible party is a person or group that may owe costs under federal or state law. Cleanup projects may now also restore water habitat, when done with the sediment work.
plaw-110-366-2008: School aid after storms gains room to bend rules under Public Law 110-366, approved on October 8, 2008. The act extends the education chief's waiver power in a 2005 hurricane relief law. One date moves from 2008 to 2009. Words that tied a second rule to two past years become for any fiscal year. A hold harmless part follows. School districts in major disaster areas named for 2008 storms, in the Midwest or the Gulf, keep at least their 2008 sums for fiscal year 2009.
plaw-110-367-2008: Defense production powers run a year longer under Public Law 110-367, approved on October 8, 2008. It is the Defense Production Act Extension and Reauthorization of 2008. The end date of the 1950 act moves from September 30, 2008 to September 30, 2009. A funding part of the same act is renewed in step, with the year 2008 struck and 2009 put in its place. Those two date changes are the whole law.
plaw-110-368-2008: One wrong word in the new 911 law is fixed by Public Law 110-368, approved on October 8, 2008. The act makes a technical correction in the NET 911 Improvement Act of 2008, passed that July. In a part of the 1999 wireless safety law, the words paragraph (2) become paragraph (3). The fix counts as if made on July 23, 2008, just after the 911 act itself took effect.
plaw-110-369-2008:
Nuclear trade with India is approved, with guard rules, by Public Law 110-369. Approved on October 8, 2008, it is the United States-India Nuclear Cooperation Approval and Nonproliferation Enhancement Act. The act approves a deal between the two countries on peaceful uses of nuclear energy.

The first title covers the approval itself. It lists policy statements, a certification duty, and pacts between India and the world atomic agency. Reporting to Congress is recast. A second title stiffens United States law on peaceful nuclear deals. It covers reprocessing deals, talks with other nations, and policy at the Nuclear Suppliers Group. The sample ends there.
plaw-110-370-2008:
Native American gifts to the nation are honored by Public Law 110-370, a joint resolution approved on October 8, 2008. It is the Native American Heritage Day Act of 2008. The part shown gives the findings behind the honor.

Native Americans are the descendants of the first people of this land, the text states. They have served in the armed forces in every war since the Revolution. In most such wars, more of them served per head than any other group, the act states. Their gifts span farming, medicine, music, language, and art. Wide honor would lift pride and self worth in Native youth, Congress adds.
plaw-110-371-2008:
Aid for the Appalachian region is renewed and improved by Public Law 110-371, approved on October 8, 2008. It is the Appalachian Regional Development Act Amendments of 2008. The purpose line in the enrolled text drops a letter, spelling the older act's name as Apalachian.

The part shown caps how much of a grant may go to office costs. Half is the normal cap. For a local district that serves a county marked distressed, the commission may allow three quarters. For a county marked at risk, the cap is a lower share, set just below that. The sample ends inside the rule.
plaw-110-372-2008: Pay for top federal specialists is recast in part by Public Law 110-372, approved on October 8, 2008. It is the Senior Professional Performance Act of 2008. The act deals with locality pay, the add-on that varies by place of work. A cap in that system is set at level III of the Executive Schedule for named classes of posts. Senior level and scientific or professional posts, under a named section, join the class list. The sample ends inside dense cross references on pay.
plaw-110-373-2008:
A national list of ALS cases is planned in Public Law 110-373, approved on October 8, 2008. It is the ALS Registry Act. ALS is amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, a disease of the nerve cells that move the muscles.

Within a year of a report named in the act, the health chief may build the list, if science backs the step. Data would cover ALS and like motor neuron disorders that are mixed up with it. The count would show how often the disease strikes and how many live with it. The list would help study links to work and surroundings.
plaw-110-374-2008:
Public Law 110-374, passed by the 110th Congress in 2008, is the Prenatally and Postnatally Diagnosed Conditions Awareness Act. It covers families who get a positive test result for Down syndrome or a like health problem before or after birth.

The act amends the Public Health Service Act to grow sound facts and support for those patients. It seeks more referrals to key support services and current facts on life outcomes, health, growth, learning, and social life. It also backs stronger support networks through federal health agencies and outreach work. The sample text ends while the new section's definitions are still being set out.
plaw-110-375-2008: Florida salvage work once needed a federal license. Public Law 110-375, from the 110th Congress in 2008, repeals one old rule in title 46 of the United States Code. It strikes section 80102, which had required a license to work in the business of salvaging on the coast of Florida. The act also removes that item from the chapter table of sections. After the change, the license rule no longer stands in federal law.
plaw-110-376-2008:
Renewing the United States Fire Administration is the job of Public Law 110-376, the act of the 110th Congress from 2008. Its findings note that fire deaths have fallen over 25 years, yet the country still has one of the highest fire death rates among rich nations.

The findings cite 3,245 civilian fire deaths in 2006, plus many fire injuries and large money losses. They also note that more than 100 firefighters die on duty each year. The act keeps the agency in place to lead work with state, local, and fire service groups. The act frames that work as a shared duty across levels of government.
plaw-110-377-2008:
Public Law 110-377, the Poison Center Support, Enhancement, and Awareness Act of 2008, came from the 110th Congress. It amends the Public Health Service Act to renew aid for poison centers across the country.

The act renews the national toll-free poison help number, a national media drive, and a grant program for poison control. Its findings call poison centers the first defense against harm and death from poisoning. They note that the public and health workers call local centers day and night for help, with more than four million calls in 2007.
plaw-110-378-2008:
Helping homeless youth is the focus of Public Law 110-378, the Reconnecting Homeless Youth Act of 2008, from the 110th Congress. The act amends the Runaway and Homeless Youth Act and clears funds for its work.

Its findings say services for young people should use a positive youth growth approach. That approach should give each young person safety and structure, a sense of belonging, and self-worth. It should also build independence, control over one's own life, and close ties with others. Later parts cover the basic center program for youth in crisis.
plaw-110-379-2008:
Public Law 110-379, the QI Program Supplemental Funding Act of 2008, was passed by the 110th Congress. It amends title XIX of the Social Security Act to add funds for the Qualifying Individual program, known as the QI program.

The act raises one funding figure from 300 million dollars to 315 million dollars. It raises a second figure from 100 million dollars to 130 million dollars. A further part requires states to use the Public Assistance Reporting Information System, known as PARIS. That system helps states check who gets public aid. The QI program helps low-income people pay Medicare costs, which is why the added funds matter.
plaw-110-380-2008: Funds for community food projects are the subject of Public Law 110-380, passed by the 110th Congress in 2008. The act says funds set aside for fiscal year 2008 shall stay open until September 30, 2009. That extra time lets the money fund proposals sought in fiscal year 2008. The act also fixes one error in an earlier farm law, changing a wrong act name back to the Food Stamp Act of 1977.
plaw-110-381-2008:
Michelle's Law, Public Law 110-381 from the 110th Congress in 2008, protects college students who must pause school for health reasons. It amends three laws: the Employee Retirement Income Security Act, the Public Health Service Act, and the Internal Revenue Code.

The act makes sure dependent students who take a medically needed leave of absence do not lose health coverage. It sets rules for when a leave counts as medically needed and how long coverage must last. In plain terms, a sick student can step away for care without at once losing a parent's health plan.
plaw-110-382-2008:
Speeding up citizenship cases for troops is the aim of Public Law 110-382, the Military Personnel Citizenship Processing Act, from the 110th Congress in 2008. Many service members file papers to become citizens while they serve.

The act sets up an Office of the FBI Liaison inside the Department of Homeland Security. That office tracks the work of the Federal Bureau of Investigation in citizenship cases. The goal is faster handling of each case. The act also sets a deadline for working through applications filed by members of the Armed Forces. Faster handling matters most to troops serving far from home.
plaw-110-383-2008:
Public Law 110-383, the Pechanga Band of Luiseno Mission Indians Land Transfer Act of 2007, was passed by the 110th Congress in 2008. It deals with federal land in Riverside County and San Diego County, in California.

The act moves that land from the Bureau of Land Management to the United States, to be held in trust for the Pechanga Band. The transfer took effect on the date the act became law, subject to valid rights held by others. Trust land is held by the federal government for the tribe's use and benefit.
plaw-110-384-2008: Public Law 110-384, the Let Our Veterans Rest in Peace Act of 2008, came from the 110th Congress. Congress finds that each cemetery should guard grave markers and that all citizens, veterans included, have earned the right to rest in peace. The act directs the United States Sentencing Commission to ensure fit punishment add-ons for people who receive stolen property when that property is a veteran's grave marker.
plaw-110-385-2008:
Better facts on broadband service are the goal of Public Law 110-385, passed by the 110th Congress in 2008. Title I carries the short name Broadband Data Improvement Act. The law seeks better federal and state data on where broadband is offered and how good it is.

Congress finds that broadband growth has helped the economy, public safety, health care, and schools. The act also backs wider spread of low-cost broadband to all parts of the nation. Good maps of current service are treated as the first step toward closing gaps in access.
plaw-110-386-2008:
Public Law 110-386, the Hydrographic Services Improvement Act Amendments of 2008, renews and amends an older water survey law. The 110th Congress passed it in 2008. The work at issue is the measuring and charting of coasts and waters.

The act rewrites key term meanings in the 1998 law. It defines hydrographic data as facts gained through water depth surveys, shoreline surveys, and remote sensing. The term also covers tide, water level, and current readings. Clear meanings matter because ships, ports, and coastal work rely on such data for safe travel. The rewritten terms also frame how survey work is classed under the act.
plaw-110-387-2008:
Care for veterans with mental health needs is the heart of Public Law 110-387, the Veterans' Mental Health and Other Care Improvements Act of 2008. The 110th Congress aimed it at post-traumatic stress disorder and substance use problems.

The act grows substance use treatment services run by the Department of Veterans Affairs. It sets rules for care for veterans who face both mental health and substance use problems. It also sets up a trial program for web-based substance use care for veterans of recent wars. A tribute to Justin Bailey opens the main title.
plaw-110-388-2008: Who appoints a top personnel chief is the whole question here. Public Law 110-388, from the 110th Congress in 2008, changes who appoints one senior staff officer. Under the act, the Secretary of Homeland Security appoints the Chief Human Capital Officer of the Department of Homeland Security. The act amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002 by striking one paragraph and renumbering the next two. That single edit is the whole law.
plaw-110-389-2008:
Public Law 110-389, the Veterans' Benefits Improvement Act of 2008, amends title 38 of the United States Code. The 110th Congress wrote it to improve pay, housing, work, school, and insurance gains for veterans.

Title I covers pay and pension matters. It deals with the notices the Department of Veterans Affairs must give claimants about proof for claims. It also covers court review of the rating schedule used for veterans' disabilities. A report on why claim outcomes vary across offices is also required, along with more time for contract medical exams. Later titles take up housing, work, school, and insurance gains in turn.
plaw-110-390-2008:
Public Law 110-390, the White Mountain Apache Tribe Rural Water System Loan Authorization Act, came from the 110th Congress in 2008. It directs the Secretary of the Interior to give a loan to the White Mountain Apache Tribe.

The loan is for planning, design, and early building work on a rural water system. The act names that system the Miner Flat Project, built around the Miner Flat Dam. It covers the dam and linked parts that supply water for home use, as set out in a project report from February 2007. The act rests on that report for the shape and scale of the system.
plaw-110-391-2008: Public Law 110-391, the Special Immigrant Nonminister Religious Worker Program Act, was passed by the 110th Congress in 2008. The act extends the special immigrant program for religious workers who are not ministers. It moves the cutoff date in the Immigration and Nationality Act from October 1, 2008 to March 6, 2009. It also orders the Secretary of Homeland Security to issue final rules within 30 days to cut or end fraud in grants of that status.
plaw-110-392-2008:
Ending tuberculosis in the United States is the stated goal of Public Law 110-392, the Comprehensive Tuberculosis Elimination Act of 2008. The 110th Congress amended the Public Health Service Act to push toward that goal.

Title I sets a national strategy through the Department of Health and Human Services and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. It covers joint work among agencies and a review of public health powers. Later parts cover research on the disease and funds cleared for the work. The act treats a full plan, not one step, as the path to ending the disease.
plaw-110-393-2008: Federal land on Front Street in Norfolk is at stake. Public Law 110-393, from the 110th Congress in 2008, deals with one piece of federal land in Norfolk, Virginia. It lets the Secretary of Commerce sell or trade land held by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration at 538 Front Street, about 3.78 acres with its buildings, to the City of Norfolk. The sale may go ahead only if the Secretary finds it serves the agency and the federal government, and first tells the named House committees.
plaw-110-394-2008:
Public Law 110-394, the National Sea Grant College Program Amendments Act of 2008, renews and amends the Sea Grant program. The 110th Congress passed it in 2008. Sea Grant links federal funds with colleges that study coasts and seas.

The act updates the findings and purpose of the older program law. New finding text backs work on how coastal areas get ready for hazards and respond to them. It names steps such as forecast, review, response, and recovery work. The rest of the act carries the detailed changes to program rules and funding.
plaw-110-395-2008: A New York post office takes the name Kenneth Peter Zebrowski. Public Law 110-395, passed by the 110th Congress in 2008, names one post office building in New City, New York. The Postal Service site at 245 North Main Street shall be known as the Kenneth Peter Zebrowski Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-110-396-2008: Naming a post office building in North Saint Paul, Minnesota is the whole job of Public Law 110-396, from the 110th Congress in 2008. The Postal Service site at 2523 7th Avenue East shall be known as the Mayor William 'Bill' Sandberg Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-110-397-2008: A Florida post office honors an Army specialist. Public Law 110-397, passed by the 110th Congress in 2008, names one post office building in Coconut Creek, Florida. The Postal Service site at 4233 West Hillsboro Boulevard shall be known as the Army SPC Daniel Agami Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-110-398-2008:
Farm payment rules for very small farms are changed by Public Law 110-398, from the 110th Congress in 2008. It amends the farm program parts of the Food, Conservation, and Energy Act of 2008.

The act pauses a ban on certain farm payments during the 2008 crop year. The ban had blocked direct payments and like aid when a farm's base acres added up to 10 acres or less. Growers may join base acres and reshape farms to deal with the rule. A like pause is written for peanuts as well. Peanuts get the same pause in their own program section of the act.
plaw-110-399-2008: A fallen Marine's name goes on a Massachusetts post office. Public Law 110-399, from the 110th Congress in 2008, names one post office building in Seekonk, Massachusetts. The Postal Service site at 156 Taunton Avenue shall be known as the Lance Corporal Eric Paul Valdepenas Post Office Building. Any mention of that site in a law, map, rule, or other federal record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-110-400-2008:
Public Law 110-400 bears the short name Keeping the Internet Devoid of Sexual Predators Act of 2008, or KIDS Act of 2008. The 110th Congress passed it to require convicted sex offenders to register their online identifiers.

The act directs the Attorney General to require each sex offender to give the registry the online names and accounts the offender uses or will use. The Attorney General decides which types of identifiers count under the Sex Offender Registration and Notification Act. The aim is to let registries track offenders online. A registry that holds online names can warn the public in new ways.
plaw-110-401-2008:
Fighting child exploitation online is the work of Public Law 110-401, the PROTECT Our Children Act of 2008, from the 110th Congress. Its full name stresses resources, officers, and new tools against cyber threats to children.

The act orders the Department of Justice to build and carry out a national strategy against child exploitation. It improves the Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force program and grows funds for regional computer forensic labs. The goal is to help police probe and charge child predators with stronger tools and teamwork. Regional labs give local police expert help with seized computers and phones.
plaw-110-402-2008: Court police powers and one job title both change here. Public Law 110-402, from the 110th Congress in 2008, does two small jobs for the Supreme Court. First, it extends the power of the United States Supreme Court Police to guard court officials away from the Supreme Court Grounds, moving the end year from 2008 to 2013. Second, it changes a job title. The Administrative Assistant to the Chief Justice becomes the Counselor to the Chief Justice, with matching edits in title 28.
plaw-110-403-2008:
Stronger remedies for theft of ideas and works are set out in Public Law 110-403, the Prioritizing Resources and Organization for Intellectual Property Act of 2008. The 110th Congress passed it to toughen both civil and criminal law in this field.

Title I deals with civil claims, covering claim registration and remedies for infringement. It raises damages in counterfeiting cases, with triple damages in some cases. It also covers the import and export of infringing goods. Later titles add criminal penalties and better coordination of federal enforcement work. Stronger civil and criminal tools sit side by side in one act.
plaw-110-404-2008:
Public Law 110-404, the Presidential Historical Records Preservation Act of 2008, amends title 44 of the United States Code. The 110th Congress cleared grants for Presidential Centers of Historical Excellence.

Under the act, the Archivist may make grants on a competitive basis, with advice from the named commission. Grants go to groups that save and open to the public the records of a former President. The aid is aimed at Presidents who do not have a presidential archival depository. Saving the papers and widening public access are the twin goals. The Archivist leads the national records system, so the grant role fits there.
plaw-110-405-2008:
Public Law 110-405, the Air Carriage of International Mail Act, was passed by the 110th Congress in 2008. It amends section 5402 of title 39 to change the rules for Postal Service air transport contracts.

The new text deals with mail flown between points in foreign air transport. As a rule, the Postal Service may contract for that flying only with certificated air carriers. The section lays out when such a contract may be awarded. The change updates how overseas mail moves by air under federal contracts. Only the foreign leg of mail flights is covered by this section.
plaw-110-406-2008:
Running the federal courts more smoothly is the aim of Public Law 110-406, the Judicial Administration and Technical Amendments Act of 2008. The 110th Congress packed many small court fixes into one act.

Early parts change the divisions of the western district of Tennessee and add an extra attendance fee for jurors on long trials. Other parts cover jury summons power, public drawing rules for jury wheels, and court technology costs. The act also repeals an old bankruptcy provision and deals with how court registry funds are invested. Small fixes of this kind keep court rules clear for judges and staff.
plaw-110-407-2008:
Public Law 110-407, the Drug Trafficking Vessel Interdiction Act of 2008, targets low-profile drug boats at sea. The 110th Congress amended titles 46 and 18 to deal with submersible and semi-submersible vessels that sail with no nationality.

Congress declares that running such a vessel on an ocean voyage is a grave world problem. It aids cross-border crime, drug trafficking, and terrorism, and it threatens safe sea travel and national safety. Title I then sets a criminal ban on running a vessel of that kind without nationality. Boats that ride low in the water are hard for patrol craft to spot.
plaw-110-408-2008: Public Law 110-408, the Criminal History Background Checks Pilot Extension Act of 2008, keeps a trial program alive for a year longer. The pilot lets volunteer groups obtain criminal history background checks. The act amends the PROTECT Act by changing a 66-month pilot period to a 78-month period. That one edit, from the 110th Congress, is the whole law.
plaw-110-409-2008:
Watchdogs inside federal agencies get stronger backing under Public Law 110-409, the Inspector General Reform Act of 2008. The 110th Congress amended the Inspector General Act of 1978 to guard their independence.

The act says each Inspector General shall be picked without regard to party ties, based only on honesty and proven skill. Skill areas named include accounting, auditing, finance, law, and investigations. The act also deals with how Inspectors General may be removed. It creates a Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency to join their work. Watchdogs who fear removal may pull back, so removal rules matter.
plaw-110-410-2008: A Pennsylvania veterans clinic takes a man's name. Public Law 110-410, from the 110th Congress in 2008, names one veterans clinic in Hermitage, Pennsylvania. The Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic there shall be known as the Michael A. Marzano Department of Veterans Affairs Outpatient Clinic. Any mention of that clinic in a law, rule, map, or other federal record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-110-411-2008:
Housing aid for Native Americans is renewed by Public Law 110-411, the Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Reauthorization Act of 2008. The 110th Congress kept those housing programs in force.

Title I covers block grants and grant rules, including Indian housing plans and the review of those plans. It also deals with program income and labor standards. Title II covers low-cost housing work, naming broad goals and which families may gain aid. The act rests on tribal self-direction in planning and running housing with federal funds. Indian housing plans are the tool tribes use to set their own goals.
plaw-110-412-2008:
Public Law 110-412 goes by the short name PRICE of Homeland Security Act. The 110th Congress passed it in 2008 to improve federal aid to state, local, and tribal governments for sharing information.

The act amends the Homeland Security Act of 2002. It clears up how grant funds under two grant sections may be used. The full name points to paying back staff costs tied to joint intelligence work. In short, grant money can support the people who share threat information across levels of government. Staff who work side by side across agencies are the focus here.
plaw-110-413-2008:
Honoring organ donors with a medal is the purpose of Public Law 110-413, the Stephanie Tubbs Jones Gift of Life Medal Act of 2008. The 110th Congress created the medal for donors and for the families of donors.

Any organ donor, or the family of a donor, may gain the medal if funds are open for it. The Secretary of Health and Human Services must direct the organ network body to set up a way to apply. The medal gives public thanks for the gift of organs that save other lives. The medal bears the name of Stephanie Tubbs Jones in its title.
plaw-110-414-2008:
Public Law 110-414, the Mercury Export Ban Act of 2008, bars the sale, spread, transfer, and export of elemental mercury. The 110th Congress acted on findings that mercury is highly toxic to people, ecosystems, and wildlife.

The findings warn that many women of childbearing age carry mercury in their blood at levels that could put a baby at risk. They also cite risk of nerve harm for many children born each year. Eating fish tainted with mercury is named as the chief source of exposure in the United States. Cutting exports aims to keep United States mercury out of world trade.
plaw-110-415-2008:
Public Law 110-415, the Methamphetamine Production Prevention Act of 2008, helps stores track sales of drug-making chemicals. The 110th Congress aimed it at electronic logbook systems for methamphetamine precursor sales.

The act clears up rules on how signatures are captured and kept in those electronic logbooks. It amends the Controlled Substances Act on sales of listed products. Buyers must show a photo ID card from a state or the federal government, or a like approved document. The logbooks help police spot bulk buying of cold drugs used to make meth. Sellers keep the logbook entries so police can trace bulk sales later.
plaw-110-416-2008:
Grants for better mental health care for offenders are renewed by Public Law 110-416, from the 110th Congress in 2008. Its long name adds the words Reauthorization and Improvement to an older crime reduction act.

The act amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968. It renews grants that join adult and juvenile programs for offenders with mental illness. It also funds better police responses to mentally ill offenders. A study and report on how common mental illness is among offenders is also called for. Better care inside the justice system is the thread through each part.
plaw-110-417-2008:
Public Law 110-417 is the Duncan Hunter National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2009. The 110th Congress used it to clear funds for military work of the Department of Defense for that year.

The act also clears funds for military building and for defense work of the Department of Energy. It sets the strengths, meaning the troop counts, for the armed services for fiscal year 2009. Its findings honor Representative Duncan Hunter, who served San Diego in the House from 1980 to the end of the 110th Congress. Yearly defense acts of this kind set policy as well as funding levels.
plaw-110-418-2008: Rapids below a torn-down dam gain a senator's name. Public Law 110-418, passed by the 110th Congress in 2008, names one stretch of river in Virginia. The manmade rapids on the Rappahannock River at the site of the former Embrey Dam in Fredericksburg shall be known as the John W. Warner Rapids. The act gives the exact spot by latitude and longitude. Any mention of that part of the river in a federal record counts as a mention of the new name.
plaw-110-419-2008: A Florida coastal unit gets fresh map lines. Public Law 110-419, from the 110th Congress in 2008, fixes the map lines for one coastal unit in Florida. It replaces the map for the Coastal Barrier Resources System Clam Pass Unit FL-64P in the official map set. The new map bears the same unit name and is dated July 21, 2005. The Secretary of the Interior must keep the map on file and open for public viewing under the Coastal Barrier Resources Act.
plaw-110-420-2008:
Medals for Native American code talkers are required by Public Law 110-420, the Code Talkers Recognition Act of 2008. The 110th Congress said their service deserves prompt honor for dedication and valor, and that such honor is long overdue.

The findings recall that when the United States entered World War I, Native Americans were not yet counted as citizens. Even so, members of Indian tribes and nations joined the Armed Forces to fight. The act honors the code talkers who used their native languages to send secret messages in war. Medals are the form of honor the act orders for each code talker group.
plaw-110-421-2008: Public Law 110-421, the Bulletproof Vest Partnership Grant Act of 2008, extends one grant program for police gear. The act amends the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968. It changes the end year for funding approval from 2009 to 2012. In plain terms, the federal grant program that helps buy bulletproof vests for officers stays cleared through fiscal year 2012. That single date change is the whole law.
plaw-110-422-2008:
Public Law 110-422 is the National Aeronautics and Space Administration Authorization Act of 2008. The 110th Congress cleared the programs of the space agency, known as NASA, for fiscal year 2009.

Title I clears the funding levels for that year. Title II turns to Earth science, covering goals for Earth watching work and the running of national Earth observation efforts. It also covers survey missions on a ten-year cycle and the move of test research into daily services. Landsat heat data continuity gets its own section. Earth science is only one part of a much wider space program act.
plaw-110-423-2008: Paper pay stubs become a choice, not a duty. Public Law 110-423, from the 110th Congress in 2008, deals with pay stubs for federal workers. Workers who get their pay by electronic funds transfer must be given the choice to get their pay stubs in electronic form as well. The Office of Personnel Management must take fit steps to make sure that choice is offered. The act defines worker and agency terms for this rule, covering staff in Executive agencies.
plaw-110-424-2008:
Training for state and local prosecutors gets federal backing under Public Law 110-424, passed by the 110th Congress in 2008. The Attorney General may award a grant to a national nonprofit group to run a national training program.

The training aims to improve the work skills of state and local prosecutors. It also aims to help federal, state, and local prosecutors work better together. Aid may support broad legal schooling in trial practice and current law. Support staff training and other help the Attorney General finds fit are also covered. The named example group is the National District Attorneys Association.
plaw-110-425-2008:
Public Law 110-425 bears the name Ryan Haight Online Pharmacy Consumer Protection Act of 2008. The 110th Congress amended the Controlled Substances Act to deal with online drug sellers.

The core rule is plain: no controlled substance that is a prescription drug may be sold or given out over the Internet without a valid prescription. The act defines what counts as a valid prescription for web sales. The rule targets web pharmacies that shipped strong drugs with no real doctor review. The sample text ends while the meaning of valid prescription is being set out.
plaw-110-426-2008:
More federal money for the organ transplant network is cleared by Public Law 110-426, the Stephanie Tubbs Jones Organ Transplant Authorization Act of 2008. The 110th Congress amended the Public Health Service Act for this purpose.

The act raises the funding figure for the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network from two million dollars to seven million dollars. It also orders a report to Congress within one year. The report must name transplant programs and give other facts about the network's work. The network matches donor organs with patients who need them. A stronger network can match donor organs to waiting patients more fairly.
plaw-110-427-2008:
Public Law 110-427, from the 110th Congress in 2008, deals with two parcels of federal land, one in Ohio and one in Minnesota. It lets the Administrator of General Services act on both sites.

For Eastlake, Ohio, the act lets the agency release deed limits on land given to the city in 1964. The site holds the John F. Kennedy Senior Center, at 33505 Curtis Boulevard, on about 10.873 acres. The act sets the terms, including what the city must give in return. A second section covers land in Koochiching County, Minnesota. Land freed of old deed limits can be put to fuller local use.
plaw-110-428-2008:
Public Law 110-428, the Inmate Tax Fraud Prevention Act of 2008, amends the Internal Revenue Code of 1986. The 110th Congress acted to help stop false tax returns filed by prisoners.

The act lets the Secretary of the Treasury share certain prisoner return facts with the Federal Bureau of Prisons. Sharing follows steps the Secretary sets. Tax return facts are kept private by law, so this act carves a narrow opening for prison officials. The goal is to spot and block fraud by inmates. Prison staff gain the facts only for the stated fraud-fighting purpose.
plaw-110-429-2008:
Transfer of naval vessels to foreign nations is cleared by Public Law 110-429, from the 110th Congress in 2008. Title I carries the short name Naval Vessel Transfer Act of 2008.

The President may transfer the named vessels to the named foreign recipients on a grant basis. The transfers rest on the Foreign Assistance Act of 1961. The value of a vessel sent as a grant does not count toward the yearly cap on transferred excess defense goods. The act names the vessels by pointing to an earlier House bill. Grant transfers give allied navies United States ships at no purchase cost.
plaw-110-430-2008: Public Law 110-430 is a joint resolution from the 110th Congress that sets two dates for January 2009. First, the first regular session of the One Hundred Eleventh Congress shall begin at noon on Tuesday, January 6, 2009. Second, the joint meeting to count the electoral votes for President and Vice President, cast by electors in December 2008, shall be held on January 8, 2009. That count date differs from the date in title 3.
plaw-110-431-2008: Legal help for crime victims gains more funded years. Public Law 110-431, from the 110th Congress in 2008, renews funding for help to crime victims. It clears funds for the National Crime Victim Law Institute to support victims under Crime Victims Legal Assistance Programs, part of the Victims of Crime Act of 1984. The act does this by editing the Justice for All Act of 2004. It swaps the years 2006 through 2009 for 2010 through 2013 in five places, moving the funding window forward.
plaw-110-432-2008:
Rail safety is the subject of Public Law 110-432, passed by the 110th Congress in 2008. Division A is the Rail Safety Improvement Act of 2008. The law amends title 49 to cut rail deaths, injuries, and hazardous material spills.

The division clears funds and sets duties for the Federal Railroad Administration. Early parts call for a rail safety strategy and a program to cut risk. A key part deals with putting positive train control in place. That system can stop or slow a train to prevent a crash. Rail lines carry both people and freight, so the stakes are broad.
plaw-110-433-2008: Election penalty power gains five more years of life. Public Law 110-433, from the 110th Congress in 2008, extends one power of the Federal Election Commission through 2013. The Commission may keep imposing civil money penalties based on a penalty schedule it sets and publishes. The act adds a clause to the Federal Election Campaign Act of 1971. It covers violations tied to reporting periods that begin on or after January 1, 2000 and end on or before December 31, 2013. A matching edit strikes an old subsection elsewhere.
plaw-110-434-2008:
Public Law 110-434, the Vessel Hull Design Protection Amendments of 2008, amends chapter 13 of title 17. The 110th Congress acted to clear up the meanings of the words hull and deck in boat design law.

The new text says the design of a vessel hull, a deck, or a hull and deck joined counts for protection. A plug or mold used to shape the boat is covered as well. The act also notes an exception for Defense Department rights in a registered design. Boat makers gain clearer cover for their hull shapes. Hull shape is a key part of a boat maker's design work.
plaw-110-435-2008:
Public Law 110-435, the Webcaster Settlement Act of 2008, amends section 114 of title 17 on music rights. The 110th Congress made room for deals on the copying and playing of sound recordings by webcasters.

The act widens who can make such deals, changing small commercial webcasters to commercial webcasters in the text. It swaps an old set of dates for a span of not more than 11 years starting January 1, 2005. It also updates the deciding body to the Copyright Royalty Judges. Web radio services gain a path to settle royalty terms. Royalty terms shape whether small web radio stations can stay on air.
plaw-110-436-2008:
Public Law 110-436 extends the Andean Trade Preference Act, as the 110th Congress voted in 2008. The program gives duty-free or favored trade terms to beneficiary nations in the Andes region.

The rewritten end-date section sets firm cutoffs by country. Favored treatment for Colombia and Peru shall not stay in effect after December 31, 2009. For Ecuador the cutoff is June 30, 2009, with a possible added span to the end of 2009. That added span turns on a review by the President of set trade criteria. Country-by-country dates show the program winding down at varied speeds.
plaw-110-437-2008:
Public Law 110-437, the Capitol Visitor Center Act of 2008, sets up the office that runs the Capitol Visitor Center. The 110th Congress placed the office inside the Office of the Architect of the Capitol.

Title I names the site as the Capitol Visitor Center and states its purposes. It also covers naming inside the center and the use of its Emancipation Hall. Title II sets up the office, led by a Chief Executive Officer for Visitor Services. The act aims at sound running of the center for the many guests who tour the Capitol.
plaw-110-438-2008:
Debt relief for called-up troops is granted by Public Law 110-438, the National Guard and Reservists Debt Relief Act of 2008. The 110th Congress amended title 11, the bankruptcy code, for a limited time.

Qualifying Guard members and reservists are freed from the means-test presumption of abuse under chapter 7. The relief covers those called to active duty or a homeland defense task after September 11, 2001. The call must last not less than 90 days. Without the shield, the means test could block a fresh start in bankruptcy court. Chapter 7 is the part of bankruptcy law for personal fresh starts.
